title: EPF and VPF — your provident fund from salary
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: If you work in a company covered by the EPF Act, 12% of your basic salary is deducted every month as the employee's contribution to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), and your employer adds a matching share (part of it goes to the pension scheme, EPS). EPF earns government-declared interest, around 8% in recent years, which is tax-free up to specified contribution limits. You can withdraw fully after you retire, or after two months of unemployment; partial withdrawals are allowed for specific needs like a home, medical emergency or marriage. VPF (Voluntary Provident Fund) lets you contribute more than 12% from your salary at the same EPF interest rate — a low-risk way to save more. Keep your UAN active and link your Aadhaar and bank account so you can track and move your PF when you change jobs.
summary_hinglish: Salary se basic ka 12% har mahine EPF mein katta hai aur company bhi barabar daalti hai. EPF ka byaj sarkar tay karti hai (8% ke aas-paas). VPF mein tum 12% se zyada daal sakte ho same byaj par. UAN active rakho aur job change par PF transfer karo.
summary_hi: सैलरी से बेसिक का 12% हर महीने EPF में कटता है और कंपनी भी बराबर योगदान देती है। EPF पर सरकार तय ब्याज देती है। VPF में आप 12% से ज़्यादा जमा कर सकते हैं। UAN चालू रखें और नौकरी बदलने पर PF ट्रांसफर करें।
